name: old asphalt road, mostly flat smooth charcoal like a modern city road: two close base greys in large soft patches with a few worn lighter spots, very sparse 1-2 pixel light aggregate flecks and rare shaded 2-pixel-wide cracks (no lane paint); its unconnected edges are a nearly straight slightly wavy broken rim into dirt, with an occasional bite, chip or short edge crack, and a dry dark-brown ledge on the south side; laid as a road network with crossroads, dead ends and long straight 1-wide and 3-wide runs that mix three edge variants
label: wasteland_ruins/asphalt

surfaces.part: asphalt road patches on dirt ground (flat terrain tileset)

answer.evidence: The image is a flat terrain sheet viewed straight down: grey asphalt road pieces (crossroads, dead ends, 1-wide and 3-wide runs) on a brown dirt background. The road is a ground surface with no standing volume, no front face and no height. The thin dark-brown ledge on the south side of the pieces is only a 1-2 row edge, not a front face of 3+ rows. For a terrain tile this flat top-down view is the intended reading, but it has no 3/4 top-plus-front structure.

styleAnswer.evidence: The asphalt ramp has only about 3 steps: one dark charcoal base, one close second grey, and the lighter worn ovals, with a few 1-pixel flecks. The big charcoal areas read as flat blocks with pale oval stamps on top, not grain. The brown dirt surround has about 3-4 tones and is better varied than the road itself. Measured facts agree: 22% near-flat coverage against 0% for both references, and only 9 distinct colours in total against 80 for the grass reference. The 5 visible tones per tile is above the grass (3) but below the paving (7). The edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so the outline is a dark material tone and is not a sticker line. The road rims are fairly clean and uniform, without the per-clump shading and tile-by-tile detail of the references. Overall it is shallower and flatter than Beodeul. The smooth flat look is intended by the brief, but it still falls below the bar, so it fails.
